questions.stem:
(a) Describe four features of the religious life of the Arabs during the Jahiliyyah. [12 marks]
(b) Explain how Islam reformed any three social practices of that period. [13 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
12 marks: any four religious features, 3 marks each - idol worship (Hubal, al-Lat, al-'Uzza, Manat) in and around the Ka'bah; belief in jinn and soothsayers (kahin); divination with arrows; sacrifices to idols; a few hunafa' holding to the faith of Ibrahim; distorted pilgrimage rites
5 marks: first reform explained - e.g. ban on female infanticide and protection of daughters
4 marks: second reform explained - e.g. limits on polygamy, rights of women including inheritance and mahr
4 marks: third reform explained - e.g. prohibition of wine, gambling, usury or tribal blood-feuds; brotherhood of faith over tribe
questions.explanation: Model answer: Pre-Islamic Arabs worshipped idols such as Hubal, al-Lat and al-'Uzza, consulted soothsayers, cast divining arrows and offered sacrifices to idols, while a few hunafa' kept to Ibrahim's monotheism. Islam forbade burying daughters alive, gave women rights of inheritance and mahr, limited the number of wives, banned wine, gambling and usury, and replaced tribal loyalty with the brotherhood of faith.

questions.stem:
(a) Give an account of the Hijrah of the Prophet (S.A.W.) from Makkah to Madinah. [15 marks]
(b) State five lessons Muslims can learn from the Hijrah. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: causes - persecution in Makkah; death of Abu Talib and Khadijah; pledges of 'Aqabah with people of Yathrib
4 marks: Quraysh plot to kill him; 'Ali sleeps in his bed; he leaves with Abu Bakr
4 marks: three days in the Cave of Thawr; the search party; spider's web/dove tradition; guide 'Abdullah ibn Urayqit
3 marks: arrival at Quba, building of the mosque, entry into Yathrib (Madinah) and warm welcome
10 marks: any five lessons, 2 marks each - trust in Allah (tawakkul); careful planning; sacrifice for faith; loyalty of friends (Abu Bakr); courage ('Ali); honesty in returning trusts; patience in persecution
questions.explanation: Model answer: Facing persecution and losing his protectors, the Prophet accepted the invitation of the Yathrib believers made at 'Aqabah. When the Quraysh plotted to kill him, 'Ali slept in his bed while he left secretly with Abu Bakr, hid for three days in the Cave of Thawr and travelled by an unusual route to Quba, where he built a mosque before entering Madinah. The Hijrah teaches trust in Allah combined with planning, sacrifice, loyalty, courage and honesty.

questions.topic: The Battles of Badr, Uhud and Khandaq
questions.stem:
(a) Narrate the events of the Battle of Badr. [15 marks]
(b) State five reasons for the victory of the Muslims at Badr. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: background - Quraysh caravan led by Abu Sufyan; Quraysh army set out to protect it; 2 A.H. (Ramadan)
4 marks: strength - about 313 Muslims against about 1,000 Quraysh; Muslims positioned near the wells
4 marks: the duels at the start (Hamzah, 'Ali, 'Ubaydah) and the general fighting
4 marks: outcome - Abu Jahl and other leaders killed; about 70 Quraysh killed and 70 captured; few Muslim deaths; treatment of captives
10 marks: any five, 2 marks each - help of Allah (angels, Q.8:9); strong faith; leadership of the Prophet; good choice of position near water; unity and discipline; overconfidence of the Quraysh
questions.explanation: Model answer: In Ramadan of 2 A.H. the Quraysh marched to protect Abu Sufyan's caravan. About 313 Muslims met roughly 1,000 Quraysh at Badr; after single combats won by Hamzah, 'Ali and 'Ubaydah, the Muslims routed the enemy, killing Abu Jahl and others and taking about 70 captives. Victory came through Allah's help, strong faith, the Prophet's leadership, a good position near the wells and discipline.

questions.stem:
(a) Discuss the achievements of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab as caliph. [15 marks]
(b) How did 'Uthman ibn 'Affan contribute to the preservation of the Qur'an? [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
15 marks: any five achievements, 3 marks each - expansion into Syria, Iraq, Persia and Egypt; Hijrah calendar; diwan (register) and public treasury; appointment of judges/separation of judiciary; establishment of garrison towns (Kufah, Basrah); night patrols and concern for the poor; title Amir al-Mu'minin; Tarawih in congregation
4 marks: differences in recitation arose in the provinces (report of Hudhayfah)
3 marks: he obtained Hafsah's copy and appointed Zayd ibn Thabit and others to make standard copies in the Quraysh dialect
3 marks: copies sent to major cities and other variant copies destroyed, uniting Muslims on one text
questions.explanation: Model answer: 'Umar expanded the state into Syria, Iraq, Persia and Egypt, introduced the Hijrah calendar, set up the diwan and treasury, appointed judges, founded garrison towns and cared personally for the poor. 'Uthman, alarmed by disputes over recitation, had Zayd ibn Thabit and others prepare standard copies from Hafsah's manuscript, sent them to the provinces and ordered other copies destroyed.

questions.topic: Spread of Islam in West Africa
questions.stem:
(a) Explain five factors that aided the spread of Islam in West Africa. [15 marks]
(b) Give an account of the role of Shehu Usman dan Fodio in the spread of Islam in Nigeria. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
15 marks: any five factors, 3 marks each - trans-Saharan trade; Muslim scholars and teachers; conversion of rulers (e.g. Mali, Kanem-Borno); Almoravid influence; intermarriage; Qur'anic schools; jihads; simplicity of the message
3 marks: preaching and teaching in Gobir and Hausaland against corruption and syncretism
3 marks: hijrah to Gudu and jihad from 1804
4 marks: establishment of the Sokoto Caliphate, emirates, Shari'ah administration and scholarly writings
questions.explanation: Model answer: Islam spread through traders crossing the Sahara, scholars and Qur'anic schools, the conversion of kings, intermarriage and later jihads. Usman dan Fodio preached against corruption and mixed practices in Hausaland, made hijrah to Gudu, launched the jihad in 1804, founded the Sokoto Caliphate with its emirates and wrote many works that strengthened Islamic learning.

questions.stem:
(a) Write out in transliteration or translation Suratud-Duha (Q.93). [10 marks]
(b) State five lessons from the surah. [15 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: correct rendering of the eleven verses - oath by the morning light and the night; your Lord has not forsaken you nor hated you; the hereafter is better than the present; your Lord will give you and you will be pleased; did He not find you an orphan and shelter you, astray and guide you, in need and enrich you; so do not oppress the orphan, do not repulse the one who asks, and proclaim the bounty of your Lord (deduct for omissions)
15 marks: any five lessons, 3 marks each - Allah does not abandon His servants; hope and patience in hardship; the hereafter is better; gratitude for Allah's favours; kindness to orphans; kindness to beggars/those who ask; speaking of Allah's blessings
questions.explanation: Model answer: The surah swears by the morning brightness and the still night that Allah has not forsaken the Prophet, promises that the future is better and that he will be satisfied, reminds him that he was an orphan sheltered, unguided then guided, poor then enriched, and commands kindness to the orphan and the one who asks and proclamation of Allah's bounty. It teaches hope, gratitude and kindness to the weak.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between Hadith and Sunnah. [6 marks]
(b) Explain the following parts of a hadith: (i) isnad (ii) matn (iii) rawi. [9 marks]
(c) Name the compilers of any four of the Six Sound Collections. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: Hadith is a report of the sayings, actions or approvals of the Prophet; Sunnah is his practice or way of life which the reports record; 3 marks for each correct definition
3 marks: isnad - the chain of narrators
3 marks: matn - the text or content
3 marks: rawi - the narrator who transmits it
10 marks: any four compilers, 3 marks each for the first two and 2 marks each for the next two - al-Bukhari; Muslim; Abu Dawud; at-Tirmidhi; an-Nasa'i; Ibn Majah
questions.explanation: Model answer: Hadith is a narrated report of what the Prophet said, did or approved; Sunnah is the practice itself that the reports convey. The isnad is the chain of transmitters, the matn the text, and the rawi a narrator. The six collections were compiled by al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi, an-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.

questions.stem:
(a) State the obligatory acts (fara'id) of wudu' according to the Maliki school. [14 marks]
(b) Mention four things that nullify wudu'. [8 marks]
(c) What is the importance of wudu' to a Muslim? [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
14 marks: seven fara'id, 2 marks each - intention (niyyah); washing the face; washing the arms to the elbows; wiping the head; washing the feet to the ankles; rubbing (dalk); continuity (muwalat)
8 marks: any four, 2 marks each - passing urine, faeces or wind; deep sleep; loss of consciousness; sexual discharge; touching the private part (with the inner hand, as in Maliki view); apostasy
3 marks: wudu' is a condition for the validity of salat and for touching the mushaf; it purifies and prepares the worshipper
questions.explanation: Model answer: The Maliki fara'id of wudu' are seven: intention, washing the face, the arms to the elbows, wiping the head, washing the feet to the ankles, rubbing the limbs and continuity. Wudu' is broken by anything leaving the private parts, deep sleep, unconsciousness and touching the private part. It is required for valid salat.

questions.topic: Articles on which Zakat is paid
questions.stem:
(a) Explain the conditions under which zakat becomes due on wealth. [9 marks]
(b) Alhaji Musa owns 50 sheep that have been with him for a full year, and savings of N3,600,000 kept for a full year. Given that one sheep is due on 40 to 120 sheep and that zakat on money is 2.5%, calculate his zakat. [8 marks]
(c) Mention four beneficiaries of zakat listed in Q.9:60. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: the owner is a free adult Muslim with full ownership
3 marks: wealth reaches the nisab
3 marks: it has been held for a full lunar year (hawl), except crops which are due at harvest
4 marks: sheep - 50 lies within 40-120, so one sheep is due
4 marks: money - 2.5% of N3,600,000 = N90,000
8 marks: any four, 2 marks each - the poor (fuqara'); the needy (masakin); zakat collectors; those whose hearts are to be reconciled; freeing captives/slaves; debtors; in the cause of Allah; the wayfarer
questions.explanation: Model answer: Zakat is due on the fully owned wealth of a free Muslim when it reaches the nisab and has been held for a lunar year (crops at harvest). Alhaji Musa pays one sheep for his 50 sheep and 2.5% x 3,600,000 = N90,000 on his savings. Beneficiaries include the poor, the needy, the collectors, debtors, wayfarers, captives, new Muslims and those striving in Allah's cause.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five conditions for a valid Nikah in Islam. [15 marks]
(b) State five duties of a wife towards her husband. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
15 marks: any five conditions, 3 marks each - guardian (wali) of the bride; two upright witnesses; dowry (mahr/sadaq); offer and acceptance (ijab and qabul); consent of the parties; both parties free from prohibited relationship; bride not in 'iddah
10 marks: any five duties, 2 marks each - obedience in what is lawful; faithfulness; care of the home and children; protecting his property; not admitting people he dislikes; good companionship; respect to his relations
questions.explanation: Model answer: A valid Nikah needs a wali for the bride, two upright witnesses, a mahr, a clear offer and acceptance, the consent of the couple and the absence of any prohibited relationship or 'iddah. A wife should obey her husband in what is lawful, be faithful, guard his property and honour, care for the home and children and treat him and his relations kindly.
